A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite repagination and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original convergence and sample-efficiency experiments on generated MDPs, plus machine replacement, water reservoir, and inventory management simulations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an expectile-parameter convergence analysis in Appendix C.2.

M1.justification: The RVI, RQI, MLMC Q-learning, and synchronous/asynchronous UBSR procedures are retained, including Algorithms 1–5. The off-policy update moves from Equation (5.1) to Equation (4.3) without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use generated MDPs and the same three application domains: machine replacement, water reservoir management, and inventory management. The new expectile sweep varies parameters within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain value iteration, risk-aware RVI, MLMC Q-learning, synchronous UBSR, and asynchronous UBSR as applicable. The application comparisons also retain the same risk-measure policies, including risk-neutral policies.

E3.justification: New Figure C.3 evaluates synchronous UBSR across expectile parameters τ = 0.1 through 0.9 and reports absolute error relative to optimal average risk against iteration count. This adds a parameter-sweep protocol and error metric; the previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an analysis of how expectile risk preferences affect convergence speed. This differs from the retained Appendix C.4 analysis of policy risk across expectile parameters. Existing sampling-rate and loss-function analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing 100-run experiments, 5th/95th percentile bands, and standard-deviation reporting are retained. No new repeated-run count, seed information, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: New Figure C.3 reports faster convergence near risk neutrality and slower convergence toward extreme expectile preferences. Existing numerical results are retained: v1 Tables 1–3 match v2 Tables 5.1, C.1, and C.2, apart from equivalent formatting such as 23.733 becoming 23.7330.

T1.justification: In Appendix B.4, the proof of Lemma B.19 corrects the derivative sign for g(x) = -ℓ(-x) and uses g instead of ℓ in the associated concavity bound. These are local mathematical corrections; the theorem statements and principal convergence assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: general risk-aware RVI, provably convergent MLMC Q-learning, and empirically validated off-policy UBSR learning. The new evidence does not expand these core claims.

C2.justification: The new Appendix C.2 discussion interprets slower convergence at extreme expectile parameters as increased computational effort from sensitivity to tail events. Existing limitations concerning MLMC resampling, finite-sample guarantees, and unproved UBSR convergence remain, with some made more prominent.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies Python 3.9, Linux, and a 64-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Section 5.3 also identifies risk-aware RVI as the algorithm used to obtain the application policies. These are additional disclosures rather than evidence of changed existing experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to entropic-risk and distributionally robust MDP research are retained. The added explanation of coherent risks' worst-case expectation representation clarifies the existing connection without changing the claimed research gap.

P1.justification: The UBSR derivation moves from Section 5.2 into new Section 4.3, leaving Section 5.2 focused on experimental comparisons. The roadmap, conclusion, and several explanations receive localized revisions, alongside grammar and acknowledgment edits; most prose and structure remain.

P2.justification: The paper is globally reformatted into NeurIPS style, changing typography, title treatment, running headers, spacing, and figure/table sizing and placement. Appendix table headings are expanded, Figure C.3 is added, and subsequent figures are renumbered. This substantially revises the document's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The corrected derivation in Lemma B.19, informative convergence-sensitivity analysis in Figure C.3, and clearer implementation disclosures provide a limited improvement in correctness, empirical understanding, and reproducibility. The central methods and existing evidence remain largely unchanged, and the acknowledged convergence and finite-sample questions remain open.
